Rashi on Eruvin 17a:13:1.hebrew: היינו תנא קמא - רבנן קמאי, דאמרי: "לא דברו בשיירא אלא בהווה", ולעולם יחיד נמי מותר:
Rashi on Eruvin 17a:13:1.english: This is the first tanna - The first Rabbis, who said: "They spoke of a caravan only in the present [as a common occurrence]," and actually an individual too is permitted.

Rashi on Eruvin 17a:14:1.hebrew: איכא בינייהו יחיד ביישוב - דתנא קמא, דקאמר לא דברו בשיירא אלא בהווה, ולעולם יחיד נמי מותר — יחיד דומיא דשיירא, דבדרך, ולא ביישוב, הואיל ויכול לעשות מחיצה הוגנת. ורבנן בתראי, אמילתיה דרבי יוסי ב"ר יהודה קא מהדרי, דקאמר איהו אינה מחיצה לא בדרך ולא ביישוב, ואמרי ליה רבנן, אחד משני דברים — או שתי או ערב — מחיצה היא, אחד יחיד ואחד רבים, בין בדרך בין ביישוב:
Rashi on Eruvin 17a:14:1.english: There is [a difference] between them [regarding] an individual in a settlement - For the first tanna, who said, “They spoke of a caravan only as the prevalent situation,” and [that] in fact an individual is also permitted — [meant] an individual similar to a caravan: [one who is] on the road, but not in a settlement, since he is able to make a proper partition. And the latter Rabbis were responding to the statement of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, who said that [such a partition] is not a partition, neither on the road nor in a settlement; and the Rabbis said to him: “One of the two things” — either warp or woof — “is a [valid] partition,” whether [for] an individual or [for] many, whether on the road or in a settlement.

Rashi on Eruvin 17a:15:1.english: In a camp - [A camp] that goes out to war.

Rashi on Eruvin 17a:15:2.english: One may bring wood - And they are not concerned about robbery.

Rashi on Eruvin 17a:15:3.hebrew: ומלערב - עירובי חצירות. אם הקיפו אלו ואלו, ומחיצה מפסקת ביניהם ויש שם פתח, אין צריכין לערב:
Rashi on Eruvin 17a:15:3.english: And from establishing an eiruv - [This refers to] eiruvei chatzerot. If these [soldiers] and those [soldiers] enclosed [their areas], and a partition separates between them and there is an opening there, they do not need to establish an eiruv.

Rashi on Eruvin 17a:16:1.hebrew: למלחמת הרשות - סתם מלחמת רשות ממלחמת יהושע ואילך, שהיא היתה מלחמת מצוה:
Rashi on Eruvin 17a:16:1.english: To an optional war - An optional war in general is from the war of Joshua onward, for that [war of Joshua] was a commanded war.

Rashi on Eruvin 17a:16:2.english: Dry wood - And all the more so moist [wood].

Rashi on Eruvin 17a:17:1.english: Ten conditions - [This is taught in] Bava Kamma, in the chapter [entitled] 'Merubah' (Bava Kamma 80b).

Rashi on Eruvin 17a:17:2.hebrew: שיהו מרעין בחורשין - שיהא כל אדם מוליך בהמותיו לרעות ביער של חברו, ולא יקפיד בעל היער, משום דלאו לקצירה קאי:
Rashi on Eruvin 17a:17:2.english: That they may graze in the woods - That any person may lead his animals to graze in his fellow's forest, and the owner of the forest shall not object, because it is not designated for harvesting.

Rashi on Eruvin 17a:19:1.hebrew: הכא בתלושין - אע"פ שתלשום הבעלים לצרכן להיסק, ויש בהם משום גזל אצל אחרים, מותר לאנשי מחנה:
Rashi on Eruvin 17a:19:1.english: Here, with detached [wood] - Even though the owners detached them for their own needs, for kindling, and there is [an element of] robbery in them regarding others, it is permitted to the members of the camp.

Rashi on Eruvin 17a:1:1.hebrew: רישא רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה - דקאמר יחיד בית סאתים, דאי רבנן, אפי' ליחיד כל צרכו יהבינן:
Rashi on Eruvin 17a:1:1.english: The first clause [is according to] Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda - For he said [that] an individual [gets] a beit saatayim; for if [it were according to] the Rabbis, even to an individual we give all his needs.

Rashi on Eruvin 17a:21:1.english: A met mitzva acquires its place - It is one of the ten conditions that Joshua stipulated.

Rashi on Eruvin 17a:2:1.hebrew: אין משום דקאי אבוה בשיטתיה - גבי יחיד, קאמר רבי יהודה נמי דאין נותנין לו אלא בית סאתים במחיצת שתי או ערב:
Rashi on Eruvin 17a:2:1.english: Yes, because his father holds in accordance with his opinion - With regard to an individual, Rabbi Yehuda also says that they give him only [an area of] two beit se'ah with a partition of warp or woof.

Rashi on Eruvin 17a:3:1.hebrew: שלשה בחמש אסורין - כלומר, פעמים ג' אנשים אסורין אפילו בחמש סאין, ופעמים שמותרים אפילו בשבע:
Rashi on Eruvin 17a:3:1.english: Three in five are prohibited - That is to say, at times three people are prohibited [from carrying] even in [an area of] five se’ahs, and at times they are permitted [to carry] even in [an area of] seven [se’ahs].

Rashi on Eruvin 17a:3:2.english: The Torah, the Prophets, and the Writings - It is an oath.

Rashi on Eruvin 17a:4:1.hebrew: מאי לאו פנוי מאדם - כגון שלשה שהקיפו ח' סאים, דכי יהבת לכל חד בית סאתים, אכתי פשו להו בית סאתים פנוי בלא בעלים. אבל ז' לא, דכי יהבת בית סאתים לכל חד, לא פש ליה אלא חד בית סאה בלא בעלים:
Rashi on Eruvin 17a:4:1.english: What, is it not unoccupied by people - For example, three [people] who enclosed eight [beit] se'ah, for when you give each one a beit satayim [an area of two se'ah], there still remains for them a beit satayim unoccupied, without owners. But [if they enclosed] seven, [it is] not [prohibited], for when you give a beit satayim to each one, there remains only one beit se'ah without owners.

Rashi on Eruvin 17a:4:2.hebrew: לא פנוי מכלים - כלומר, שיש בין המחיצות בית סאתים פנוי שלא היו צריכין לו. ואע"ג דאינהו שלשה, אם אין צריכין אלא לבית סאתים והקיפו ד' סאין — נמי בטלי מחיצות:
Rashi on Eruvin 17a:4:2.english: No, unoccupied by utensils - That is to say, there is between the partitions an unoccupied [space of] two beit se’a that they did not need. And even though they are three [people], if they need only two beit se’a and they enclosed four se’a, the partitions are likewise nullified.

Rashi on Eruvin 17a:6:1.english: And one of them died - On the day of Shabbat.

Rashi on Eruvin 17a:6:2.english: And [others] were added to them - On Shabbat.

Rashi on Eruvin 17a:6:3.hebrew: שבת גורמת - שלשה ומת אחד מהן, הואיל וגורמת שבת להתיר, מותרין השנים, אפי' לר' יהודה. שנים והקיפו יותר מבית סאתים, אע"פ שניתוספו עליהן דיורין, אסורין לרבי יהודה, הואיל וכשנכנסה שבת גרמה לאיסור:
Rashi on Eruvin 17a:6:3.english: Shabbat determines - [If there were] three, and one of them died: Since Shabbat determines [the status] to permit [it], the two are permitted, even according to Rabbi Yehuda. [If there were] two, and they enclosed more than a beit satayim: Even though [additional] residents were added to them, they are forbidden according to Rabbi Yehuda, since when Shabbat entered, it determined [the status] to be forbidden.

Rashi on Eruvin 17a:6:4.hebrew: דיורין גורמין - ג' ומת אחד מהן, דבצרי דיורין — אסורין אם הקיפו יותר מבית סאתים. שנים ונתוספו עליהן — מותרין, דאיכא דיורין:
Rashi on Eruvin 17a:6:4.english: The residents determine [the status] - [If there were] three and one of them died, since the residents have decreased, they are forbidden [to carry] if they enclosed more than a beit se'atayim. [If there were] two and [others] were added to them, they are permitted, since there are [sufficient] residents.

Rashi on Eruvin 17a:7:1.hebrew: עירב דרך הפתח ונסתם הפתח - אם היו ב' חצרות ופתח ביניהם, ועירבו דרך הפתח, ונסתם הפתח; או אם היו ב' חנויות ופתח ביניהם, דעירבו על דעת הפתח, ועכשיו נסתם בשבת — שנפלה כנגדו מפולת:
Rashi on Eruvin 17a:7:1.english: [If one] established an eiruv via the opening and the opening was sealed - If there were two courtyards with an opening between them, and they established an eiruv via the opening, and the opening was sealed; or if there were two shops with an opening between them, where they established an eiruv relying on the opening, and now it was sealed on Shabbat — as a mound of rubble fell in front of it.

Rashi on Eruvin 17a:7:2.hebrew: מהו - מי שרי לאשתמושי דרך שאר חלונות הפחותות מד', שאין ראויות לעירוב, כדאמרי' בפ' חלון (לקמן עירובין דף עו.):
Rashi on Eruvin 17a:7:2.english: What is [the halakha] - Is it permitted to make use [of them] through the other windows that are less than four [handbreadths], which are not fit for an eiruv, as we say in the chapter [entitled] “Chalon” (below, Eruvin 76a)?

Rashi on Eruvin 17a:8:1.english: A courtyard that was breached - On Shabbat.

Rashi on Eruvin 17a:8:2.english: From two of its sides - It is explained in the chapter 'Kol Gagot' (ibid., 94b) why [the mishna] specified 'from two of its sides'.

Rashi on Eruvin 17a:8:3.english: Whose cross beam or side post was removed - On Shabbat.

Rashi on Eruvin 17a:8:4.english: [They are] permitted for that Shabbat - For we say: Since it was permitted [at the onset of Shabbat], it remains permitted [for the rest of that Shabbat].

Rashi on Eruvin 17a:9:1.hebrew: רבי יוסי אומר אם מותרין כו' - ומפרשינן בפ' כל גגות (שם ד' צה.) דר' יוסי לאיסור, והכי קאמר: כשם שאסורים לעתיד לבא, כך אסורין לאותה שבת. אלמא, לא אמרי' הואיל והותרה הותרה כדרבי יצחק:
Rashi on Eruvin 17a:9:1.english: Rabbi Yosei says: If they are permitted, etc. - And we explain in the chapter Kol Gagot (ibid. 95a) that Rabbi Yosei [spoke] to prohibit, and this is what he is saying: Just as they are prohibited in the future, so too are they prohibited on that Shabbat. Evidently, we do not say "since it was permitted, it remains permitted" in accordance with [the view of] Rabbi Yitzchak.

Tosafot on Eruvin 17a:19:1.hebrew: התם במחוברים - להאי שינויא נמי איירי בהיזמי והיגי, דלא התקין יהושע אלא היזמי והיגי המחוברים ולחים, כדאמר בהדיא במרובה (ב"ק דף פא.):
Tosafot on Eruvin 17a:19:1.english: "There, [it is] with attached [wood]" - According to this resolution as well, [the Gemara] is speaking of thorns and shrubs [hizmei vehigei], for Joshua instituted [his ordinance] only for thorns and shrubs that are attached and moist, as [the Gemara] states explicitly in [the chapter] Merubeh (Bava Kamma 81a).

Tosafot on Eruvin 17a:7:1.hebrew: עירב דרך הפתח - נראה לר"י דהלכה כרב הונא, דשבת הואיל והותרה הותרה, דתניא כוותיה בפרק הדר (לקמן עירובין ד' ע:): "כל שהותר למקצת שבת כו'". ואין לומר דרבי יצחק יעמיד הברייתא אליבא דרבי יהודה — דהא מוקי נפשיה אפילו כר' יהודה בשמעתין; ואביי נמי סבירא ליה הכי בפרק כל גגות (לקמן עירובין ד' צג:). ומיהו היכא דליתנהו למחיצות — אסור, כדמסיק הכא: "אנא דאמרי אפי' כר' יוסי, עד כאן לא קאמר רבי יוסי אלא משום דליתנהו למחיצות". ורב נמי פסיק כרבי יוסי בסוף פרק כל גגות (שם), וכן שמואל בנפרצה לרה"ר. ואע"ג דרב פסיק כר' יוסי אפי' באיתנהו למחיצות, כדמוכח גבי שתי חצירות ונפל כותל שביניהם — דהתם הוי שפיר איתנהו למחיצות, דאכתי איכא מחיצות חיצונות שעל ידיהן נעשה החצר רה"י, ומשום הכי מייתי מחצר [גדולה] שנפרצה על בעיא דרב הושעיא בפרק כל גגות (עירובין ד' צג:) — מ"מ נראה דבהא הילכתא כרב הונא, כדפרישית. ונראה לר"י שאם עירבו לצורך שניהן מבית לבית ונסתם הפתח בשבת, דשרי כרב הונא; ואפילו נסתם באמצע השבוע ואח"כ נפתח בשבת — שרי, דחזר העירוב למקומו. וראיה מדאמר בפ' הזורק (שבת ד' קא:): "ספינות קשורות זו בזו מערבין ומטלטלין מזו לזו, נפסקו נאסרו, חזרו ונתקשרו חזרו להתירן הראשון". ועוד, דלמסקנא דשמעתין, דמוקי ר' יצחק נפשיה כר' יהודה ושרי אפי' במבוי שניטלה קורתו, כ"ש דיתיר בעירבו דרך הפתח; דהא בפרק הדר (לקמן עירובין ד' ע:) קאמר: "כל שהותר למקצת שבת כו'" — לאתויי עירב דרך הפתח, "וזה הכלל" — לאתויי מבוי שנטלה קורתו, משמע דאי לא דתני "זה הכלל", לא הוי שרינן מבוי שניטלה קורתו, אע"ג דהוי שרינן עירב דרך הפתח ונסתם. וריצב"א אומר דמהתם נמי יש להוכיח דהלכה כרב הונא, דההיא סוגיא כרב הונא, דקפיד אמחיצה טפי, כדאמר הכא: "עד כאן לא קאמר רבי יוסי כו'", ולהכי אי לאו "זה הכלל" לא הוי שרינן מבוי שניטלה קורתו, אע"ג דשרינן עירב דרך הפתח ונסתם, דאילו רבי יצחק קפיד טפי אדיורין:
Tosafot on Eruvin 17a:7:1.english: If one established an eiruv via the opening - It appears to the Ri that the halakha is in accordance with Rav Huna, that since Shabbat was permitted, it was permitted [and remains so], as it is taught in accordance with his view in a baraita in the chapter [entitled] "Hadar" (below, Eruvin 70b): "Whatever was permitted for part of Shabbat [is permitted for the entire Shabbat]..." And one cannot say that Rabbi Yitzḥak would establish the baraita in accordance with [the view of] Rabbi Yehuda [and therefore reject it], for he establishes his own view [as agreeing] even with Rabbi Yehuda in our sugya; and Abaye also holds this way in the chapter [entitled] "Kol Gagot" (below, Eruvin 93b). However, where the partitions are no longer [present], it is prohibited, as [the Gemara] concludes here: "It is I who stated [my view] even according to Rabbi Yosei; Rabbi Yosei stated [his view] only because there are no [longer] partitions [intact]." And Rav also rules in accordance with Rabbi Yosei at the end of the chapter [entitled] "Kol Gagot" (ibid., 95a), and so too Shmuel in [the case of a courtyard whose partition] was breached into the public domain. And even though Rav rules like Rabbi Yosei even where partitions are present, as is proven regarding two courtyards [where] the wall between them collapsed — for there, partitions are indeed present, since there are still outer partitions through which the courtyard is rendered a private domain, and for this reason [the Gemara] cites from "a [large] courtyard that was breached" [into a small one] regarding the dilemma of Rav Hoshaya in the chapter [entitled] "Kol Gagot" (Eruvin 93b) — nevertheless, it appears that in this [matter], the halakha is in accordance with Rav Huna, as I explained. And it appears to the Ri that if they established an eiruv for both of their needs from house to house, and the opening was sealed on Shabbat, it is permitted, in accordance with Rav Huna; and even if it was sealed in the middle of the week and was subsequently opened on Shabbat, it is permitted, as the eiruv returned to its place. And a proof is from that which [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] "HaZorek" (Shabbat 101b): "Boats tied to one another: [the occupants] may establish an eiruv and carry from one to another; if they became untied, they are prohibited; if they were re-tied, they return to their initial permitted status." And furthermore, according to the conclusion of our sugya, where Rabbi Yitzḥak establishes his own view in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, and [Rabbi Yehuda] permits even in [the case of] an alleyway whose crossbeam was removed, all the more so would he permit where they established an eiruv via the opening! For in the chapter [entitled] "Hadar" (below, Eruvin 70b), [the Gemara] says: "Whatever was permitted for part of Shabbat..." — [this comes] to include one who established an eiruv via the opening [and the opening was sealed]; "This is the general rule" — [this comes] to include an alleyway whose crossbeam was removed. This implies that were it not that [the baraita] taught "This is the general rule," we would not have permitted an alleyway whose crossbeam was removed, even though we would have permitted one who established an eiruv via the opening and it was sealed. And the Ritzba says that from there too it can be proven that the halakha is in accordance with Rav Huna, for that sugya is in accordance with Rav Huna, who is more particular about partitions, as [the Gemara] says here: "Rabbi Yosei stated [his view] only..." And therefore, were it not for "This is the general rule," we would not have permitted an alleyway whose crossbeam was removed, even though we permitted one who established an eiruv via the opening and it was sealed; whereas Rabbi Yitzḥak is more particular about residents.

Tosafot on Eruvin 17a:8:1.hebrew: קורותיו או לחייו - בפירוש רש"י בכתיבת ידו נמצא כתוב: "קורתו או לחיו", והדין עמו. ואע"ג דאליבא דרבי יהודה קיימינן, ואשכחת לה לדידיה מבוי ניתר בשתי קורות או שני לחיים, כמו במפולש — מ"מ למה לי למינקט "קורותיו", כיון דבקורה אחת או בלחי אחד נאסר המבוי:
Tosafot on Eruvin 17a:8:1.english: "Its cross beams or its side posts" - In Rashi's commentary in his own handwriting, it was found written: "Its cross beam or its side post", and he is correct. And even though we are standing according to [the view of] Rabbi Yehuda, and according to him you can find that an alleyway is rendered permissible with two cross beams or two side posts, such as in an open-ended [alleyway] — nevertheless, why did [the mishna] need to state "its cross beams," since the alleyway becomes prohibited with [the removal of] one cross beam or one side post?
